title: MPI Collectives with Programmable Smart Switches
problem: MPI collective operations are critical for HPC and ML training but incur significant latency and bandwidth overhead. Smart network switches could offload these operations to the network hardware, but integration is lacking.
motivation: Programmable smart switches are widely deployed in cloud data centers but underutilized in HPC. They provide opportunities for offloading MPI collectives (especially reductions) closer to the network, reducing latency and improving throughput.
method: mpitofino moves MPI collective operations—where multiple computers coordinate to combine or share data—from running in software on individual computers to running directly on the network switch hardware (an Intel Tofino ASIC). The system uses P4, a programming language for network chips, to specify what operations the switch should perform, and leverages existing RoCEv2 and RDMA capabilities on network cards to enable direct memory access. By integrating into Open MPI, the system lets existing parallel computing applications automatically benefit from network-level coordination without requiring code changes.
key_novelty: mpitofino is the first practical implementation of MPI collective operations on a programmable Ethernet switch (Intel Tofino), using P4 with RoCEv2 and RDMA support.
contributions: mpitofino prototype for MPI collective offloading
P4 programming of reduction operations on Tofino ASIC
Integration with RoCEv2 protocol and RDMA hardware
Demonstration of data throughput near 100GBit/s line rate
Scalable reduction performance on Ethernet fabric
limitations: Requires programmable switch hardware; P4 has computational constraints; may not benefit all MPI operations; integration complexity with existing MPI implementations.
